Source images (gitignored): /Users/kyle/code/discord/discord-bot/screenshots/2026-09-30-characters-runes/ (01 to 37). This capture is not a game update — the source names no game version, so no entry or custom fact carries a game_version.

skill_levels.1: Summons 1 [Hawk Sprite] upon entering battle: Auto-attacks the nearest enemy, dealing 60% of character ATK DMG and applying [Hunt Mark]. [Hunt Mark]: Sprite DMG taken +15%.
skill_levels.2: After an enemy with [Hunt Mark] has been hit by Sprite attacks 10 times, triggers [Grand Hunt]: Summons (5 + Current Sprite count on map) Phantom Hawks that dive at the target in sequence, each dealing 60% of character ATK DMG.
skill_levels.3: When [Grand Hunt] ends, triggers [Hawk Dive]: Summons a Phantom Hawk to dive at the target, dealing 200% of character ATK DMG to all enemies along its path and applying [Hunt Mark]. If target dies during Grand Hunt, all remaining unsummoned Phantom Hawks are converted into [Hawk Dives], each targeting a different enemy. When Grand Hunt ends, own ATK increases by [30% + 5% x No. of enemies with Hunt Mark on the map (up to 3 counted)] for 10s.
skill_levels.4: Weapons can fight independently and count as Sprites when calculating Sprite count on the map. Sprite DMG +20%. Additionally, Sprite DMG +20% for each enemy marked with [Hunt Mark] on the map, up to 3 enemies.

star_system.max_stars: 8. A hero (character) goes up to 8 stars. The Characters screens of Morty, Rick, Artemis and Wukong (all Legendary), captured 30 September 2026, each show a row of 8 star slots under the hero's name and a Star-up Stats list with one card for each star from 1 to 8. The original source record (contributed 4 August 2026) gives the same 8-star ladder for every hero ('Every hero has 8 star tiers'), so answer 8 stars for Rare and Epic heroes too. This is the hero star count; skin star levels and the other star counts in this knowledge base are separate systems.

star_pattern.8: Skill Level 4 (8 stars is the maximum)

star_system.skill_level_unlocks: Skill Lv1 at 0 stars (just owning the character), Skill Lv2 at 2 stars, Skill Lv3 at 5 stars, Skill Lv4 at 8 stars. Star 7 gives only the [All] stat boost — Skill Lv4 comes at star 8, the final star. Skill level is separate from star/character level. The Star-up Stats list prints the LV.2 text on the 2-star card, the LV.3 text on the 5-star card and the LV.4 text on the 8-star card on all four hero screens captured 30 September 2026 (Morty, Rick, Artemis, Wukong — all Legendary); where the skill panel was captured it labels Lv.2 'Unlocks when character is 2-Star' and Lv.3 'Unlocks when character is 5-Star'. The original source record (contributed 4 August 2026) gives the same stars — 0, 2, 5 and 8 — for every hero. When a member asks what a hero's skill does 'at N stars', answer with the skill level reached at that star count: Lv.1 at 0 or 1 stars, Lv.2 at 2 to 4 stars, Lv.3 at 5 to 7 stars, Lv.4 at 8 stars — give that level's text first and the lower levels as what the hero already has.
star_system.note: Stars 1, 4, and 7 give the same stat boost per character (e.g. Alex gets [All] Max HP +3% each time). Stars 3 and 6 each unlock a resonance slot (the star-up cards print 'Resonance Unlock' at 3 stars and 'Resonance Slot +1' at 6 stars). Star 7 gives the stat boost only; skill level 4 comes at star 8, the final star (Star-up Stats of Morty, Rick, Artemis and Wukong, captured 30 September 2026).
star_system.how_stars_are_earned: Stars are unlocked by collecting hero shards; the hero's Characters screen shows a shard counter. Counters observed: 0/50 on heroes at 0 stars (Rick, Artemis and Wukong, captured 30 September 2026) — consistent with the 50 shards recorded here both for acquiring a hero and for its first star; '0 + 20/100' on Morty at 3 stars (same capture; what the leading '0 +' counts is not explained on the screen); and 'X/150' or 'X/100' on hero cards in an earlier record that did not note the hero or star level. The shard cost of each later star and the total needed to reach 8 stars are not documented — say so and point at !suggest.

runes.enchantment_stats: Blessing, Enhancement and Ability Runes also have another layer of Enchantment Stats; Etched Runes do not (guild owner XYIAN, 30 September 2026: enchants are found on non-etched runes; the Etched popups captured that day show an Unequip or Swap button and no Enchant button, while the Ability and Blessing popups show Unequip and Enchant). Enchantment Stats have multiple categories depending on the type of rune (see enchantment_categories), with only one enchantment selected at a time on a single rune; a Twinborn rune's popup showed two Enchantment Stats lines (see enchantment_system.one_at_a_time). Enchants have to be rolled for: per XYIAN (30 September 2026) it is a random process that uses 1,000 Enchantium a roll — the Standard Enchantizer's cost (standard_enchantizer) — with a chance of higher-level (higher-rarity) enchants at low rates. Enchantment colours follow the normal rune tier colours — grey Common, green Fine, blue Rare, purple Epic, yellow Legendary, red Mythic — and red is the best.

category_roles.etched_runes: High-power category amplifiers that lock in build identity. They multiply what your Ability Runes produce, and some Etched tiers also add effects of their own: Arrow of Echoes' Legendary line is 'Starting Skill: Diagonal Arrow', Echo Scythe's Epic line gives main weapon attacks a chance to fire [Echo Scythes], and Sprite's Awe's Mythic line carries two effects of its own — read them from the etched_sprites ladder, not from here (ladders: etched_main_weapon, etched_sprites).

stat_unlock_mechanics.dot_tiers: Dots represent only the 6 named tiers: Common, Fine, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic. A lock icon means not yet unlocked. The rune popup prints no tier names on these rows; the dot colour is the tier: grey/white = Common, green = Fine, blue = Rare, purple = Epic, yellow = Legendary, red = Mythic (confirmed by guild owner XYIAN, 30 September 2026). On Etched Runes the rows for Legendary +1, Legendary +2 and Legendary +3 carry a marker numbered 1, 2 and 3, between the yellow Legendary row and the red Mythic row, and the number badge on the rune icon is the copy's + level (a copy badged 'Legendary +2' shows rows 1 and 2 unlocked and row 3 locked). stat_unlock_mechanics.primary_stat_row: The top row shows the cumulative primary stat (knife icon = ATK PWR, heart icon = Max HP), which scales through every tier including the + variants and Mythic. Figures seen at the top of the guild owner's own copies on 30 September 2026 — examples at that copy's rarity, not tier lines: Arrow of Echoes (Etched, a Legendary +3 copy) ATK PWR +3,600 and Max HP +14,400; Echo Scythe (Etched, a Legendary +1 copy) ATK PWR +2,100 and Max HP +8,400; Healing Sprite (Ability, a Mythic copy) Max HP +6,000; Twinborn - Twin Meteors (Ability, a Mythic copy) Max HP +12,000; Blessing runes: see blessing_rune_primary_stats. twinborn_runes.what_it_is: A Twinborn rune is one rune made by combining two runes. XYIAN (guild owner), 30 September 2026: Twinborn runes are 'a rare rune type that's unlocked after obtaining your first Mythic rune, in which you can combine two runes of the same type and shape'. The one captured Twinborn popup ('Twinborn - Twin Meteors') is headed 'Ability Rune', not a category of its own; the rune categories recorded here remain the four: Etched, Blessing, Enhancement, Ability. Community facts call making one Twinborn forging or merging; the update 1.1.7 note calls it Twinborn Rune fusion. It is NOT the Rune Workshop's Fusion (rune_workshop), which fuses owned runes into one higher-rarity rune.
twinborn_runes.unlock: Twinborn unlocks after you obtain your first Mythic rune (XYIAN, 30 September 2026; also a community fact of 2026-07-29). A separate community fact of 2026-07-29 says the merge 'can be done from Legendary rarity or higher'; what that rarity refers to, and how it relates to the first-Mythic unlock, is not documented. When asked what is needed to make a Twinborn rune, give both statements and point at !suggest for how they fit together.
twinborn_runes.pairing_rule: The two runes must be of the same type and the same shape (XYIAN, 30 September 2026). Each rune category has its own icon shape (equip_slots.icon_shapes_and_screen_positions), so 'same shape' reads as the same rune category; he did not define 'type' or 'shape' further. Being in the same category is NOT known to be enough: community facts of 2026-07-29 say Twinborn forging can only be done with specific runes. Pairings recorded so far, each two runes of the same theme: the Main Weapon Etched runes Echo Scythe and Arrow of Echoes (XYIAN, 30 September 2026); 'frost shock rune can only be merged with flamenox' (community fact, 2026-07-29; both are Elemental-theme rune names); and 'Twinborn - Twin Meteors', whose lines name the Meteor Ability runes Star of Time and Star of Fury although its popup does not say which two runes were merged. Whether any other pair works, including two runes of different themes, is not documented — do not say it can; say so and point at !suggest.
twinborn_runes.cost_in_twinborn_cores: A Twinborn merge costs Twinborn Cores plus scraps. Twinborn Cores, as stated by XYIAN (guild owner) on 30 September 2026: 160 for an Etched rune (diamond icon); 80 for a Blessing rune (round icon); 40 for an Enhancement rune (left side of the Runes screen) or an Ability rune (right side). Scraps, per a community fact of 2026-07-29: made by salvaging runes; the amount is not documented. In his words the Core cost goes 'x2 x2 x2 per rarity'; the figures he gave are the three above — 40, 80, 160. Whether the cost also changes with the rarity tier of the runes being merged is not documented — point at !suggest. The same community fact says Twinborn Cores are given from events or bought in the store.

An Etched rune copy is received at one of three rarities: Rare (blue) or Epic (purple) from every shop and event that gives Etched runes, or Legendary from one real-money bundle only (US$100 as the owner stated it — the price printed in game was not captured; 'which you can pick which ones you want'; once a month; the bundle's name and shop tab are not documented, so do not name one). You never receive a copy below Rare, though Etched runes do have Common and Fine tiers and those stat lines apply. A copy can go higher than the rarity it was received at: the owner's own Etched copies captured on 30 September 2026 are badged Legendary up to Legendary +3.
